- `hue` - Color encoding for additional categorical/continuous variable
- `histplot()` - Bar-based frequency distributions with flexible binning
- `kdeplot()` - Smooth density estimates using Gaussian kernels
- `ecdfplot()` - Empirical cumulative distribution (no parameters to tune)
- `displot()` - Figure-level interface for univariate and bivariate distributions
- `pairplot()` - Matrix of pairwise relationships across dataset
- `stripplot()` - Points with jitter to show all observations
- `regplot()` - Axes-level regression plot with scatter + fit line
- `residplot()` - Residual plot for assessing model fit
- `robust` - Use robust regression (less sensitive to outliers)
- `center` - Value at colormap center (for diverging colormaps)

content.value_statement: Statistical plotting choices can slow data analysis and figure production. This skill guides Seaborn plot selection, parameters, styling, and examples for clear Python visualizations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Seaborn function and objects interfaces for statistical plotting.
Maps analysis goals to scatter, line, distribution, categorical, regression, and matrix plots.
Provides examples for faceting, grids, semantic mappings, themes, and palettes.
Guides figure export and Matplotlib customization for publication outputs.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for legends, labels, sizing, colors, and KDE bandwidth.
limitations: Does not execute Python or validate generated plots against real data.
Requires users to supply clean DataFrames and correct column names.
Covers Seaborn concepts, not full statistical modeling or hypothesis testing.
Does not include dashboard frameworks beyond notebook-oriented examples.

use_cases.title: Explore Dataset Relationships
use_cases.description: Select scatter, pair, distribution, and heatmap views for a first pass over tabular data.

use_cases.title: Prepare Publication Figures
use_cases.description: Plan polished statistical figures with consistent themes, palettes, annotations, and export settings.

use_cases.title: Compare Models or Experiments
use_cases.description: Visualize grouped outcomes, residuals, dose response, and time series with appropriate statistical summaries.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Plot Type
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner plot selection for one analysis question.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have columns [columns] and want to understand [question]. Recommend the best Seaborn plot and explain the key parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an EDA Figure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate exploratory analysis across several variables.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an exploratory visualization plan for this dataset summary: [summary]. Include plot types, variable mappings, and what each plot should reveal.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Figure for Publication
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced styling and export guidance for a finished chart.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Seaborn figure plan for publication: [description]. Recommend theme, palette, labels, annotations, and export settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Panel Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced figure design that combines several statistical views.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-panel Seaborn workflow for [research question]. Include faceting, plot types, statistical summaries, and checks for readability.

output_examples.input: User asks how to compare measurements across treatment groups with repeated observations.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a paired trajectory view plus a distribution comparison. It explains grouping, hue, error bars, and label cleanup.

output_examples.input: User needs a visual summary of correlations across numeric variables.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a correlation heatmap with a centered diverging palette, annotations, masking, and square cells for readability.

output_examples.input: User wants a presentation-ready time series chart with multiple sensors.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a faceted line plot with confidence bands, clear date formatting, legend placement, and presentation context styling.

best_practices: Start with tidy long-form DataFrames and meaningful column names.
Use figure-level functions for faceting and axes-level functions for custom layouts.
Set theme, palette, context, labels, and export settings before sharing final figures.
anti_patterns: Using unnamed arrays when labels and grouping columns are available.
Encoding too many variables with hue, size, style, rows, and columns at once.
Treating automatic confidence intervals as proof of causation.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create Seaborn statistical visualizations for exploratory analysis, comparisons, regressions, heatmaps, and publication figures.

faq.question: Does it run Seaborn code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but the user runs Python in their own environment.

faq.question: Can it help choose between plot types?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps analysis goals and variable types to suitable Seaborn plots and parameters.

faq.question: Does it cover the objects interface?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for the modern seaborn.objects API and layered plot construction.

faq.question: Can it help with publication styling?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers themes, palettes, contexts, labels, annotations, and high-quality export options.

faq.question: What data format works best?
faq.answer: Long-form DataFrames work best because they support flexible variable mapping, grouping, and faceting.
